To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fear of reinjury, psychosocial issues and the social milieu of an athlete are very important factors affecting the outcome in competitive athletes who undergo ACL reconstruction.
the key factors affecting return to sports are fear of reinjury, psychosocial issues, knee instability and pain.
the key to successful return to sports is to have a good knee outcome score, a good psychosocial status and a good relationship with the coach and teammates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors that are relevant to return to sports in athletes after ACL surgery.
the functional outcome of ACL reconstruction in competitive athletes at 5-year follow up.
the factors which affect the return to sports after ACL reconstruction in athletes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the outcome scores of the patients do not reflect their overall satisfaction or return to sports and vice versa.
a return to the preinjuring sporting levels is possible in the majority of the patients, but a fall in the sporting levels is also common and is not necessarily due to the knee outcome score.

ACL reconstruction in the competitive athlete is a successful procedure in terms of the outcome scores, but the return to preinjury levels or even the return to competitive sports is not always the case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fear of reinjury and instability are very important factors that affect the overall outcome of surgery and return to sports.
the outcome scores are not the only parameters to judge the success of the surgery.

the outcome scores of the knee do not reflect the actual functional outcome of the surgery and that a more detailed assessment of the patient's social status and psychosocial milieu should be undertaken in order to get a more accurate idea of the functional outcome of ACL surgery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a good functional outcome is not always synonymous to a good functional outcome in the sporting sense.
the patient should be counselled about the same and the surgeon should be aware of the same.
the surgeon should be aware of the psychosocial issues in athletes and should be prepared to deal with them in the postoperative period.
